newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strike still halts loading at Brazil's Santos.
newsitem.headline: Strike still halts loading at Brazil's Santos.

text.p: A strike by stevedores continued at Brazil's key port of Santos on Thursday, paralysing most loading operations except for a few vessels, including one loading orange juice, a port official said.
The stevedores began striking at 0700 local/1000 GMT on Wednesday and are expected to continue until Saturday. The strike is set to spread to the national level on Friday.
They are protesting against a ruling which allows company workers from steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to operate Cosipa's private terminal at the port.
"The strike continues. If there are no discussions it will continue through tomorrow," a spokesman at the port authority said.
There were 15 vessels docked at the port's terminal and four at private terminals. Only four vessels were loading, three with cargoes of fuels and chemicals and one with orange juice.
"The Bebedouro is loading 13,100 tonnes frozen concentrated orange juice at the Cargill point on the public quays," the spokesman said.
Ten vessels were expected to arrive.
